pr_body:
Add the `k_heap_calloc` function. Equivalent to the standard C `calloc` function.

Closes #79417.
pr_comments:
On Tue, 8 Oct 2024, Simone Orru wrote:

> I see that `k_heap_alloc` is a wrapper for `k_heap_aligned_alloc` with `align` set to  `sizeof(void *)`.
> I would use `sizeof(void *)` for memsetting. 
> What do you think about it?

I think this is wrong. In fact I'm not sure I understand the initial 
comment either.

You should zero the requested memory not more. The user is not expected 
toconsume more memory than it asked. The fact that the allocator may 
round up the allocation is an internal detail that no one should rely 
upon.

> On Tue, 8 Oct 2024, Simone Orru wrote: I see that `k_heap_alloc` is a wrapper for `k_heap_aligned_alloc` with `align` set to `sizeof(void *)`. I would use `sizeof(void *)` for memsetting. What do you think about it?
> I think this is wrong. In fact I'm not sure I understand the initial comment either. You should zero the requested memory not more. The user is not expected toconsume more memory than it asked. The fact that the allocator may round up the allocation is an internal detail that no one should rely upon.

I can revert the change. But let's first make sure which one of the two is the correct implementation.
In terms of logic, I agree with @npitre.
From the C 11 standard:
> The calloc function allocates space for an array of nmemb objects, each of whose size
is size. The space is initialized to all bits zero.

It does not help much, but fyi.
Part of me thinks not zeroing out the whole block may have security implications. Maybe it's not an issue.

On Tue, 8 Oct 2024, Daniel Leung wrote:

> Part of me thinks not zeroing out the whole block may have security implications. Maybe it's not an issue.

Security critical code should normally zero its memory before freeing 
it. You can't count on the next memory requestor to do it for you. And 
in that case, too, you're not supposed to access beyond what you 
initially asked for.

calloc() is just a convenience for getting already zeroed memory.

> E.g. the case that Daniel pointed out regarding `memset()`.

As mentioned, that particular case is wrong.

> There seems to be quite a bit of unnecessary code-formatting changes. Please only change code that is relevant to the PR.

The format changes in `subsys/tracing/sysview/tracing_sysview_ids.h` are all related to the alignment of defines. 
Since my changes are only to some of those defines if I only perform alignment for my changes it will result in a header which is partially aligned.
Formatting changes are in their own commit. So feel free to review them stand-alone.
Sure - as long as it's a separate commit, that's ok.

issue_context.title: kernel: Missing calloc equivalent funciton
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The Zephyr kernel contains various allocation functions: `k_heap_alloc`, `k_heap_realloc`, `k_heap_free`, etc.
Those can be seen as wrappers to the standard C functions `malloc`, `realloc`, `free`, etc.
However, there is no equivalent function to `calloc`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An additional allocation function could be added alongside the already present ones.

review_comments: This may not work correctly if the allocation alignment is bigger than `(num * size)`. For example, you need 2 bytes but the alignment is 8 bytes (pointer size for 64-bit system), this memset will not clear the last 6 bytes.

I see that `k_heap_alloc` is a wrapper for `k_heap_aligned_alloc` with `align` set to  `sizeof(void *)`.
I would use `sizeof(void *)` for memsetting. 
What do you think about it?

After first checking for overflow, Using `bounds` in `memset()` looks fine to me.

Can this one be resolved?
